second_order: turning a giant-logo idea into pixel work
theme_note: These codes all make the proposed NIN mark doable: testing the cooldown and available people, choosing a start point, sharing a grid, clearing a side and reporting progress. What varies is whether the turn doubts feasibility, corrects a rule, lays out the order of work or performs the work.

second_order: working with nearby fanbases so both sides survive
theme_note: These codes make or maintain reciprocal ties around neighbouring art: not overwriting Radiohead, trading spare pixels, accepting offers, returning help and carrying requests among Radiohead, Tagpro, Mexico, Tool and others. What varies is whether the turn negotiates, promises, thanks, asks or reports mutual protection.

second_order: making the mark look recognisably NIN
theme_note: These codes choose and refine what to draw: a white background, official spacing, With Teeth styling, an updated version, a Broken cover or a second HTDA mark. What varies is whether a design is adopted, deferred to avoid conflict, or rejected because the space and support are not there.

second_order: guarding the logo against vandalism and the void
theme_note: These codes perform defense rather than alliance-making: watching for hours, maintaining positions, fixing damage, warning of the void, and spending a final pixel on NIN. What varies is the threat named and whether people watch, repair, warn, order or recount their defense.

second_order: arguing whether place belongs in r/nin or one sticky
theme_note: These codes police the venue: some call the posts spam or circle-jerk material, one attacks the logo in spite, others defend the fun, and several ask moderators to collect the talk in a sticky or move coordination to Discord. What varies is exclusion, rebuttal, moderation request and relocation.

second_order: catching up people who missed what place was
theme_note: These codes arise when participants say they do not understand or missed the activity and others explain the canvas, the cooldown, community marks and the NIN–Radiohead team-up. What varies is the form of confusion and how much of the event or alliance the answer reconstructs.

second_order: celebrating the logo and the run that made it
theme_note: These codes publicly mark accomplishment: declaring the logo done or perfect, thanking helpers, sharing its making, smiling, praising the result and calling it a good run. What varies is whether the celebration concerns completion, collective effort, an image of the process or a proposed next build.

second_order: making the damaged ending feel properly NIN
theme_note: These codes turn an imperfect final image into a fitting NIN outcome through glitch aesthetics, song and release references, pride, humour and acceptance. What varies is whether damage is mourned, blamed, measured, made into a lyric joke, or preferred as more recognisably NIN.

second_order: keeping April Fools going with familiar NIN jokes
theme_note: These codes enact r/nin's separate April Fools conduct, not the canvas: remembering Strobe Light, extending its fake history, replacing Survivor with a prank record, posting a future remaster and baiting readers with a removed fake encounter. What varies is remembrance, elaboration, format-switching, bait and argument over whether the joke is worn out.

second_order: folding tile-fighting into the Survivor finale
theme_note: This single code keeps the ordinary Survivor format running while briefly recruiting r/place by telling readers they can place tiles and fight the machines. It belongs with no other practice closely enough to merge.
